nodes.statement: For integer r≥0 and real x>0, define G₀(x)=exp(−x) and, for r≥1, Gᵣ(x)=1/(r−1)! ∫₁^∞ exp(−xy)(log y)^(r−1) dy/y. Define its value to be 0 when x≤0. These kernels evaluate odd central derivatives of weight-two L-functions.

Compare log y with y−1 to obtain the explicit majorant Gᵣ(x)≤exp(−x)/x^r; use positive integrands for strict positivity.

nodes.title: Split-prime size bound
nodes.statement: Let K be imaginary quadratic with fundamental discriminant −d, d>4, and h=classNumber K. If the natural prime p splits in K, then p^h≥d/4.
hypotheses: [Field K], [NumberField K], [Algebra ℚ K], finrank ℚ K=2, discr K=−d.
p is a natural prime and the associated quadratic character has χ(p)=1.
proofSteps: A prime ideal 𝔭 of norm p has 𝔭^h principal because its class has order dividing the cardinality h.
Write a generator as (a+b√(−d))/2 with integers a,b of the appropriate parity. Its norm is p^h.
The distinct conjugate prime ideals force b≠0; therefore 4p^h=a²+db²≥d. Handle d=3,4 separately wherever an application needs them.

sources.match: The ideal-class order bound gives the quantitative obstruction to a small split prime.

acceptance: For h=3, every prime p with 4p³<d is inert or ramified.

nodes.title: Quadratic character and Liouville agreement
nodes.statement: For K as in split-prime-size, if 1≤n<(d/4)^(1/h) and gcd(n,d)=1, then χ_K(n)=λ(n), with λ the existing Liouville arithmetic function. Every prime divisor of n is inert, so the equality also holds on all products of primes below the same split-prime threshold.
hypotheses: d>4; h=classNumber K; n positive; gcd(n,d)=1.
proofSteps: Apply split-prime-size to each prime divisor of n. The size hypothesis rules out χ(p)=1 and coprimality rules out χ(p)=0.
Use complete multiplicativity of the quadratic character and existing Liouville function, including prime powers and n=1.

sources.match: A small class group makes the quadratic character imitate Liouville on a controlled range.

acceptance: The coprimality hypothesis is necessary: a ramified prime has χ(p)=0 but λ(p)=−1.

nodes.title: Positive Mellin comparison
nodes.statement: Let a≥0,m≥2 and let μ_j,ν_j be positive measures supported on (0,∞), with finite mass on every (0,t]. Their Mellin transforms converge on a common line Re(s)=σ>a, and each product (s−a)^−m∏_j μ̂_j(s), respectively (s−a)^−m∏_j ν̂_j(s), is absolutely integrable on that line. Suppose ∫₀ᵀ μ_j((0,t])dt≤∫₀ᵀ ν_j((0,t])dt for every T≥0 and each j. Then the inverse Mellin transforms of (s−a)^−m∏_j μ̂_j(s) and (s−a)^−m∏_j ν̂_j(s) are nonnegative and ordered in the same direction. All multiplicative-convolution/Fubini integrals must be absolutely integrable. The assertion includes the single-measure comparison; pointwise cumulative-mass domination is a sufficient special case.
hypotheses: Finite number of positive measures; finite mass on every (0,t], integrated cumulative-mass domination, Mellin-transform convergence and absolute integrability of the completed products on the displayed line, and multiplicative-convolution/Fubini integrability.
a≥0 for the decreasing convex comparison; m≥2; x>0.
proofSteps: Express the inverse transform as the integral of I_{a,m}(x∏t_j) against the product of the measures. Justify Fubini from the stated absolute-integrability bounds.

For fixed positive x, the kernel is nonnegative, decreasing and convex on (0,∞), with compact support towards infinity. Its distributional second derivative is a positive measure; include the boundary atom when m=2. Represent the kernel by positive hinge functions (u−t)₊. Tonelli identifies each hinge integral against μ with ∫₀ᵘ μ((0,t])dt and gives the single-factor inequality from the integrated hypothesis.
Apply that comparison one factor at a time in a finite multiplicative convolution. Integrating a pointwise cumulative inequality first gives its corollary.

Apply the integrated form to the nonaxial lattice-counting measure and its area majorant; do not assume a pointwise lattice-counting estimate. Gamma and discrete coefficient comparisons retain all normalization factors.

sources.match: O85 Lemma 3 uses integrated cumulative-mass domination and convex positive kernels; this is the hypothesis supplied by the nonaxial area estimate.

nodes.title: Goldfeld reflection contour identity
nodes.statement: Suppose F is entire, F(s)=F(2−s), F has a zero of order at least three at 1, and F decreases faster than every inverse power of |Im s| on each bounded vertical strip. For σ>3/2, (2πi)^−1∫_{Re s=σ} F(s)/(s−1)^3 ds=0, the line being oriented upwards. With F=d^(s−1)M^sΓ(s)^2Ψ(s)G(s), this is Oesterlé’s fundamental identity.
hypotheses: The entire function has the stated vertical-strip bounds; its vanishing assertion is about the actual analytic function.
d>0,M>0 in the factored form.
proofSteps: Reflection about 1 makes the vanishing order even, hence at least four, so division by (s−1)^3 leaves an entire function.
Integrate on a finite rectangle symmetric about Re s=1. The existing cycle residue/Cauchy theorem gives zero; vertical-strip decay sends the horizontal sides to zero.
Reflect the left side onto the right side and check the sign from the odd denominator; their equality forces the right line integral to vanish.

nodes.title: The truncated Euler-product residue
nodes.statement: Assume C4: Ψ is holomorphic on an open neighborhood of Re(s)≥1 with Ψ(1)=0 and Ψ′(1)≠0. Let G_U=∏_{p≤U}G_p with the C2 local roots, U≥1. Set γ(s)=M^sΓ(s)^2 and H(s)=γ(s)Ψ(s)/(s−1), with its removable value at 1; c₁=H(1)≠0,c₂=H′(1)/H(1). The residue at 1 of d^(s−1)γ(s)Ψ(s)G_U(s)/(s−1)^3 is c₁G_U(1)[log d+G_U′(1)/G_U(1)+c₂]. A contour Δ making the source indentation just to the left of 1 gives J(U) equal to this residue plus the Δ integral; the latter has absolute value at most c₃ sup_Δ |G_U|, where c₃ depends only on Ψ,M and the fixed indentation.
hypotheses: d>4,M>0,U≥1; all roots of each C2 numerator and denominator have norm at most √p.
Choose the indentation in the holomorphy neighborhood and avoid all local-factor poles; its near-center half-width is at most 1/4.
proofSteps: At 1 each denominator is nonzero since √p/p<1. Expand the product of d^(s−1), H and G_U to first order to compute the second-order pole residue.
Apply the existing residue theorem to the truncated rectangle, then pass to the limit with the gamma/Ψ strip decay.
Bound the remaining contour integral by the integral of |γΨ(s)(s−1)^−3| on Δ times sup|G_U|.

nodes.title: The three positive remainder estimates
nodes.statement: Under C1–C2, with d>4,U≥1 and γ=M^sΓ(s)^2, let G*=G−G_U and J* be the fundamental contour with G*. Then |J*|≤J₁+J₂+J₃ with the nonnegative integrals in O85 (3.4.4)–(3.4.6). Writing h=classNumber K and summing over all reduced positive-definite forms of discriminant −d, J₁≤(M/96)h²U^−1/2(|log(dM/U)|+3)^4, J₂≤(2π⁴/3)M^(3/2)h∑_q a(q)^−1, and J₃≤4π²e M^(3/2)max(2,log(4M))h²d^−1/2.
hypotheses: C1 means coefficient-wise absolute domination, with absolute convergence on the specified half-planes; a bound on numerical function values is insufficient.
K imaginary quadratic, fundamental discriminant −d; reduced forms and their normalized partial-zeta decomposition are imported.
proofSteps: Shift s by 1/2 and dominate the remaining Euler coefficients by the square of ζ_K(s)/ζ(2s), discarding the pairs a(q)a(q′)<U removed by the truncation.
Use the integrated positive Mellin comparison to replace nonaxial lattice measures by their area majorant and ζ(2s) by its square-pushforward comparison. This produces exactly the three terms.
Evaluate the gamma kernel/residue for J₁; use the elementary vertical integrals (3.4.8) and (3.4.9) for J₂ and J₃. The absolute value around log(dM/U) is required.

For the nonaxial measure use support t≥A₀=√d/2 and ν=(π/2)δ_A₀+(π/√d)·volume restricted to [A₀,∞). Its cumulative mass is (πt/√d)1_[A₀,∞)(t), so the imported integrated area bound is precisely the comparison hypothesis; its Mellin transform is (π/2)·s/(s−1)·A₀^−s for Re(s)>1.

sources.match: The coefficient and positive-measure comparisons give these explicit, uniform remainder estimates.

nodes.title: Oesterlé’s effective technical theorem
nodes.statement: Fix M>0 and Ψ satisfying C1 for Ψ and C4. For every imaginary quadratic K of fundamental discriminant −d, d>4, and Euler quotient G satisfying C1 for G, C2 and C3, there exists a uniform C>0, depending only on Ψ and M, such that C h(K)≥min(1,∏_{p∈P(d)} |G_p(1)|/(1+p^−1)) log d. C is effectively obtained from certified presentations of M, the C4 simple-zero coefficient and neighborhood, and all strip/integral bounds used in the proof. It is independent of G, K and h.
hypotheses: C1: Ψ≪ζ(2s−1)^2, G≪(ζ_K(s−1/2)/ζ(2s−1))², with absolute convergence for Re(s)>1 and >3/2 respectively.
C2: G_p(s)=(1+αp^−s)(1+βp^−s)/((1+α′p^−s)(1+β′p^−s)), all four root norms ≤√p.
C3: F=d^(s−1)M^sΓ(s)^2ΨG is entire, rapidly decreasing on vertical strips, F(s)=F(2−s), and ord₁F≥3.
C4: Ψ is holomorphic on a neighborhood of the closed right half-plane, has a simple zero at 1, and γΨ decreases rapidly on its bounded vertical strips.
proofSteps: Choose U=(√d/2)^(1/m), where m is the least positive integer satisfying m²+m≥h/2 except h=4 uses m=3/2. The split-prime bound implies at most one split prime ≤U; genus theory puts the largest ramified prime above U.
Apply the four estimates (3.5.1)–(3.5.4) to the form sum, |G_U(1)|, Re(G_U′/G_U)(1) and sup_Δ|G_U|. Combine the residue identity with J(U)=−J*.
For d≥exp(λh), bound α₅/α₆≤1+c₇(λ) with α₆>0 and c₇(λ)→0. The source formulas provide C=max(λ,c₅(1+c₇(λ))/|c₁|). For d<exp(λh), use log d<λh directly.
Retain a computable modulus and enclosure for every constant in this choice; bare analyticity does not constitute an algorithm to recover C from an arbitrary function oracle.

sources.match: A fixed Ψ and scale M control every discriminant and varying Euler quotient.

acceptance: The constant carries no dependence on d,G or the varying class number; h=4 uses the stated nonintegral m.

nodes.title: Independent arithmetic rank certificates
nodes.statement: The ℤ-finrank of E₁₃₉(ℚ)/tors is 3. For E₅₀₇₇, the affine points P₀=(0,2),P₁=(1,0),P₂=(2,0) form a ℤ-basis of E₅₀₇₇(ℚ); the torsion is trivial and the rank is 3. nodes.title: Certified odd central derivatives
nodes.statement: Let f be a normalized weight-two newform of level N with real coefficients a_n, Fricke sign giving root number −1, and |a_n|≤τ(n)√n. Let L be its actual entire L-function. For odd r≥1 with ord₁L≥r, L^(r)(1)=2r!∑_{n≥1}(a_n/n)G_r(2πn/√N). For truncation B the absolute tail is at most 2r!∑_{n>B}τ(n)n^−1/2 exp(−αn)/(αn)^r, α=2π/√N; bound this tail by an explicit geometric bound after a verified monotonicity threshold. Rational enclosures of each finite term give certified central derivative boxes. For root number +1, the central-value formula is L(1)=2Σ(a_n/n)exp(−2πn/√N), with the same coefficient tail at r=0; this supplies the explicit −7 auxiliary twist certificate.

The formula for L^(r) requires all lower derivatives to vanish; applying it to r=3 before L′(1)=0 would compute a completed-derivative expression instead.

Apply the BGZ kernel bound to the coefficient-wise tail, with divisor estimates and an explicit threshold for geometric comparison.
Evaluate exp/log/π and G_r by the imported validated-numerics interface. For 5077, first evaluate r=1; after exact vanishing, use r=3 and enclose L‴(1)/3! in (173/100,174/100).

nodes.title: Exact vanishing from a Heegner height gap
nodes.statement: Suppose a Gross–Zagier specialization gives L′(E,1)L(E^χ,1)=c·ĥ(P), where c>0, P lies in the specified rational Mordell–Weil group, the twisted central value is nonzero, and every non-torsion point has ĥ(P)≥δ>0. If a certified enclosure gives |L′(E,1)L(E^χ,1)|<cδ, then P is torsion and L′(E,1)=0. If rootNumber E=−1 this raises ord₁L(E) from at least one to at least three.

Use the trace, not the averaged Heegner point; ĥ_K for 2(O) equals twice the existing canonicalHeight under the stated field-relative normalization.

All inequalities are about the actual continued L-functions; δ is a proved gap, not a floating estimate of a regulator. For E₅₀₇₇ use χ_{−7}, conductor 248773 for the twist, certify 4<L(E^χ,1)<5 using a 2048-term exponential central-value sum with tail <10^−8, and prove the native height gap δ=1/4 from BGZ’s complete height-below-one enumeration and its three generator height enclosures.

A non-torsion P would contradict that inequality; torsion has exactly zero canonical height by the existing height API.
Since the twisted value is nonzero, deduce L′=0. Root-number parity then gives central order≥3.

nodes.title: The conductor 37 Heegner trace vanishes
nodes.statement: For the unique weight-two newform f in the relevant conductor-37 negative-Fricke eigenspace (root number +1), K=ℚ(√−139), and the normalized Heegner divisor on X₀(37), its f-isotypic trace is zero. The η quotient u(z)=η(z)^2/η(37z)^2 has divisor 3(0)−3(∞); the principal divisor of u−u(x) is the sum of the three Heegner points minus 3(∞). Consequently Gross–Zagier gives L′(1,f⊗χ_{−139})=0 after a certified L(f,1)≠0.
hypotheses: The Heegner field has discriminant −139 and class number 3; 37 splits in K.

The modular-unit/CM supplier proves u(x)∈H, u(x)^12=λ^12 for λ=(3+√−139)/2∈K of norm 37, Galois equivariance and exact divisor multiplicities. Here H is the Hilbert class field, [H:K]=3; control roots of unity in H rather than only units of K.
proofSteps: Import the modular η quotient, its cusp divisor and the CM twelfth-power relation. Since K=ℚ(√−139) contains neither i nor a primitive cube root of unity, adjoining either has degree 2 over K and cannot lie in the degree-3 extension H/K. Thus the twelfth roots of unity in H are ±1 and every CM value lies in {λ,−λ}. Galois equivariance and the orbit of size 3 force a single common value fixed by Gal(H/K), hence in K.
Subtract that common value and prove the divisor has exactly the three CM points and the order-three pole at infinity, including multiplicities. This makes the trace divisor principal in J₀(37).
Apply the classical Gross–Zagier formula to the trivial trace and divide by the nonzero conductor-37 value; transfer to the −139 twist.

This is the referenced proof of the first curve’s vanishing Heegner point.

nodes.title: Goldfeld’s modular analytic system
nodes.statement: Let f be a normalized rational weight-two newform of conductor N with ord₁L(f)≥3. For imaginary quadratic K of discriminant −d, gcd(d,N)=1 and χ_K(−N)=1, set M=N/(4π²), Ψ=L(f)L(f⊗λ), G=L(f⊗χ_K)/L(f⊗λ). Interpret the Liouville series and quotients first on their common convergence half-plane and then meromorphically, with the ramified factors retained. These data satisfy C1–C4. In particular Ψ has a simple zero at 1 because its symmetric-square factor is nonzero there and ζ(2s−1)^−1 has a simple zero; this remains true if ord₁L(f)>3.
hypotheses: The symmetric-square continuation, finite bad factors, Petersson-value identity and strip estimates are imported from AL.3.
The product completion has plus sign because χ_K(−N)=1; a rank-three curve alone does not remove this local-sign hypothesis.
proofSteps: Use L(Sym² f,2s)=∏_{p|N}(1−p^(1−2s))·ζ(2s−1)·Ψ(s), the O85 (2.3.1) normalization. Confirm every p|N correction before solving for Ψ.
Use Hasse bounds and multiplicativity for C1; compare the local ratio with quadratic-character Euler factors for C2.
The completed product is d^−1Λ(f)Λ(f⊗χ), hence entire with plus reflection and order≥3. The symmetric-square quotient yields C4 and the certified positive c₁.

The C1–C4 proof uses these actual bad factors. For fixed f the possible local conductor types and scales M form a finite list, so a common maximum of the technical constants controls every such K.

Retain the sign condition and the actual newform twist conductor Nχ.

Identify the corrected degree-four completion with d^−1Λ(f)Λ(f⊗χ), preserving C3 and its central order.
Check C4 for each corrected Ψ using the fixed finite Euler factors and symmetric-square value; enumerate all possible M and take a certified common constant.
